title: Red night mode leaves the Moon phase disc near-white — a dark-adaptation flare on the default screen
summary: MoonCard handed its painter a hardcoded `Color(0xFFD6DCE2)` in every theme, so the ~50 px solid lit limb stayed off-white (measured luminance 219) while the rest of the red-night dashboard was red-shifted. The lit colour now goes through SkotiqChartColors.forTheme(moonLitGrey, colors) — the app's existing red-night mapper, which is the identity in dark/light and re-expresses the source luminance on the red axis under red night. The dark limb and rim were already theme-driven. _MoonPainter became MoonPainter (@visibleForTesting) so the test can read the colour the card actually passes.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/moon_card_red_night_test.dart -> 'red night does not paint the moon in off-white' (red dominates green and blue, luminance below the off-white), 'every other theme keeps the neutral lunar grey'
revert_check: Replaced `litColor: SkotiqChartColors.forTheme(moonLitGrey, colors)` in moon_card.dart with `litColor: moonLitGrey`. 'red night does not paint the moon in off-white' FAILED; the dark-theme test still passed. Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: Timezone picker is inert: every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
summary: The verifier's correction was the real cause. An earlier wave had already made the PICKER honest (kUtcOffsetTimezones + kLegacyIanaUtcOffsets migration, so the stored label is one clockProvider parses), but no surface consulted clockProvider: the status-bar chip formatted `DateTime.now()` and the Dashboard header chip formatted `observationTimeProvider.time`, both host-local — which is why even 'UTC', the one label the parser accepted, changed nothing. Both chips now render `clockProvider.fromUtc(<instant>)`: the same instant re-expressed in the chosen zone. I then extended it to the rest of the clock FACES on the same screen — the night-timeline axis labels (Sunset / Astro dark / Astro dawn / Sunrise), the 'Sunset at HH:MM' countdown headline and the Moon card's moonrise/moonset — because fixing only the two chips would have put two zones side by side on one dashboard, which is worse than the uniformly host-local screen it replaced. Durations ('Astro dark in 1h 24m') and the timeline geometry are differences and therefore untouched, and observationTimeProvider still carries the true instant, so the sky maths is unchanged; only what the operator reads moves. computeNightCountdown takes `Clock clock = const SystemClock()`, so its existing pure tests keep asserting host behaviour.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/status_bar_timezone_test.dart -> 'the status-bar clock follows the chosen site timezone', '"Use system time" leaves the status-bar clock host-local', 'the dashboard header clock follows the chosen site timezone' (the offset under test is derived from the host's own offset + 5 h at run time, so the expected reading can never coincide with host-local on any machine). packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/widgets/standby/night_timeline_test.dart -> 'the sunset clock face follows the chosen site timezone'.
revert_check: (a) Restored `final displayNow = now;` (temperature_and_time.dart) and `final now = timeState.time;` (dashboard_header_actions.dart): both timezone tests FAILED, the system-time control still passed. (b) Restored `final shown = t;` inside night_timeline's `_clock`: 'the sunset clock face follows the chosen site timezone' FAILED, the other 4 countdown tests passed. Both restored -> test/screens/shell 86/86 and test/screens/dashboard/widgets/standby + moon card 13/13 green.
caveats: Clock FACES on the dashboard and the shell now share one zone. Timestamps elsewhere in the app (Analytics session tables, FITS headers, log lines) were outside this finding's evidence and were not swept; FixedOffsetClock is a fixed offset with no DST rule, which the Timezone row's own subtitle states.

title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database ... and the failure dialog contradicts itself
summary: Two halves, one already closed. The cross-database half was fixed before this wave (resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory anchors the checkpoint on the open database's folder plus a checkpoints/ subdir; adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint migrates the old support-dir file only when SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is unset) and is covered by checkpoint_directory_test.dart — verified, left alone. The self-contradiction was still live: on ANY failure the modal printed the raw caught object ('Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from') directly above the unconditional sentence 'The checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh', and offered a Retry that could only fail again. runAppCheckpointRecovery now takes a `checkpointStillResumable` probe (production: backend.getCheckpointInfo()?.canResume), re-reads it after every failed attempt and passes a CheckpointAttemptFailure to the dialog; the dialog states what is true now, drops the Retry action when the checkpoint is no longer resumable, and renders the error through describeCheckpointFailure() so a Dart wrapper never reaches the operator. A probe that itself throws is read as 'not resumable' (conservative).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/checkpoint_recovery_dialog_test.dart -> 'a checkpoint that cannot be resumed is not called available', 'the failure reads as a sentence, not as a Dart object', 'a failed attempt re-reads whether the checkpoint survived', 'a probe that itself fails reports the checkpoint as unusable', plus the pre-existing wedge tests. app_startup_checks_test.dart updated for the new signature.
revert_check: Put back the unconditional message (`'${failure.error}\n\nThe checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh.'`) and made the Retry action unconditional. 'a checkpoint that cannot be resumed is not called available' and 'the failure reads as a sentence, not as a Dart object' both FAILED. Restored -> whole test/screens/shell suite 86/86 green.
caveats: The header's frame count still comes from the checkpoint file rather than the database. With the checkpoint now anchored beside the open database that is the same run's own record, so it is no longer a cross-database claim.

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to a location the page never names and offers no way to change
summary: Both reproduced halves are already closed, and I backed out my own addition rather than duplicate one. (1) Path: resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() resolves 'backups/' beside the resolved database file, so SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is honoured — fixed before this wave and confirmed live by the verifier. (2) Disclosure: wave 3 added a 'Backups' row to Files & Storage carrying the real path (asked of backupServiceProvider.getBackupDirectory(), so it cannot drift), the sentence that 'Maximum backups' deletes the oldest bundles from that folder, and an Open folder / Copy path action. I first added a second 'Backup folder' row to the Automatic Backups > Status section — the surface the verifier cited — then removed it: Settings > Files & Storage is FilesAndStorageSettings (merged_sections.dart:99-105), which renders FilePathSettings and AutoSaveSettings on ONE page, and AutoSaveSettings has no other call site in the app. The Status section the verifier read is three sections below the row that already names the folder, so a second copy states the same path twice on one scroll and adds nothing.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/file_path_backup_folder_test.dart -> 'the backup folder is named on the page', 'the row says retention deletes from that folder', 'the folder can be opened from the row', 'an unresolvable folder still states the retention policy'. Green (7/7 with the hydration suite).
revert_check: Done on the wave-3 fix while verifying it, via its own test: the four file_path_backup_folder_test cases fail without the row. My own added row was reverted permanently for the duplication reason above (with its test — both were green before removal).
caveats: Deliberately NOT built: a user-selectable backup folder. That needs a new persisted setting plus BackupService write/list/restore plumbing — a feature — and neither reproduced defect (undisclosed path, ignoring the configured data dir) survives without it. Flagged for the owner rather than half-built.

title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Backup & Restore says a real timestamp
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave and verified here, cause and all. auto_save_settings.dart:170 now watches autoSaveLifecycleProvider — the only provider that loads the persisted `autosave.*` keys and calls start(config, lastBackup) — instead of the raw autoSaveServiceProvider, whose instance is rebuilt on every backend swap with compiled-in defaults and a status that says the machine has never been backed up; and the Status card reads autoSaveStatusProvider (auto_save_service.dart:762-780), which backfills lastBackup from the persisted `autosave.last_backup_at`, the same key Backup & Restore reads. The two surfaces now share one source, so they cannot disagree.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart -> 'Status shows the persisted last backup, not "Never"' (seeds autosave.last_backup_at 2 h old, asserts '2h ago' and that neither 'Never' nor 'Pending' renders), plus the schedule-hydration and no-clobber tests. 4/4 green.
revert_check: Pointed the page back at the raw service (`ref.watch(autoSaveServiceProvider.select((s) => AsyncValue.data(s))).when(...)` in place of `ref.watch(autoSaveLifecycleProvider).when(...)`). The suite FAILED. Restored -> 4/4 pass. The wiring is genuinely severed by the test.

title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' for an address nothing can connect to
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave at BOTH levels the finding named, verified here. (a) ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart `_discoverAddressDevices` no longer catches — it returns `discover()` directly, so the bridge's SkotiqError::connection_failed reaches the dialog and its catch branch is reachable code again. (b) indi_server_dialog.dart sets `_statusSuccess = n > 0`, so an empty probe can never render the green tick: it reads 'No INDI devices at <host>:<port>. If indiserver is running there, it has no drivers loaded — otherwise check the host and port.', and a thrown probe reads 'No response on <host>:<port>. <error>'.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/equipment/indi_server_dialog_test_connection_test.dart (stub DeviceService returning [] / a device / throwing). Green.
revert_check: Changed `_statusSuccess = n > 0;` to `_statusSuccess = true;` in indi_server_dialog.dart. The suite FAILED. Restored -> green.

title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave exactly where the verifier said the decision lives, verified here. The connect dialog records whether it is displacing a local FfiBackend (`hadLocalBackend`, connection_settings.dart:557-560) and, when the handshake fails, calls _restoreLocalBackend() -> backendProvider.notifier.useLocalBackend() before reporting 'Connection failed: <e>\nStill working locally on this computer.' A restore that itself fails is named rather than hidden. Separately, the Connection page now renders a 'Work Locally' row whenever the backend is disconnected on a desktop platform, which is the missing UI caller for useLocalBackend() the verifier flagged. `backendProvider.notifier.connect` has exactly one other caller in the whole app — the explicit --remote-host startup path in apps/desktop/lib/main.dart, where remote IS the requested mode.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_settings_local_fallback_test.dart -> 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode', 'a disconnected desktop is offered a way back to local mode'. Green.
revert_check: Replaced `final restoreError = hadLocalBackend ? await _restoreLocalBackend() : null;` with `final String? restoreError = null;`. The suite FAILED. Restored -> green.

title: The Alpaca server address can never be set
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave, verified here. connection_settings.dart:196-218 renders an 'Alpaca Server Address' row with the live `${alpacaServerHost}:${alpacaServerPort}` subtitle and a Configure button opening AlpacaServerDialog (connection_settings_alpaca_dialog.dart), which validates the port and writes through setAlpacaServerHost/setAlpacaServerPort — the core setters the finding showed had zero UI callers. It sits directly above the 'Query Alpaca on startup' toggle whose subtitle refers to 'the configured Alpaca server', so that sentence now has a referent.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_alpaca_address_test.dart -> 'the Alpaca address is shown and can be changed', 'a malformed port is refused rather than coerced'. Green.

title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so 'capture folder' returns no match
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave, verified here. settings_screen.dart:178 splits the query on whitespace and requires EVERY token to match (`tokens.every((token) => sectionMatchesToken(section, token))`), sectionMatchesToken adds kSettingsSearchSynonyms — which carries exactly the app's own vocabulary for this feature ('capture folder', 'capture directory', 'save path', 'image folder', 'disk space', 'free space', 'storage location') for files-storage — and settingsMatchRank orders an exact section title above a row title that merely contains the query. SettingsSectionDef.matches (settings_catalog.dart:79-88) is still the per-token predicate, which is correct: the tokenisation is the caller's job.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/settings_search_query_test.dart -> 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting', 'every token still has to match something', 'an autofocus term does not land on Files & Storage', 'the best match is listed first', + index-hygiene tests. Green.

title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place
summary: Fixed by an earlier wave on all three points the finding raised, verified here. The row is titled 'Detect Location' with the subtitle 'Device GPS if this machine has it, otherwise a city-level estimate from your IP address'; a consent dialog names the third-party services (ipapi.co, falling back to ip-api.com) and the ~10 km accuracy BEFORE any request leaves the machine; and the elevation is no longer inherited blindly — location_settings.dart computes the great-circle distance from the stored site and keeps the elevation only within 25 km, otherwise clearing it to the app's own 0 m 'not set' value and saying so in the snackbar ('Elevation cleared to 0 m — enter the elevation for this site.').
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/location_settings_truth_test.dart -> 'is not labelled GPS', 'asks before anything leaves the machine', 'a fix at another site clears the inherited elevation', 'a fix at the same site keeps the elevation'. Green.

title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima
summary: Fixed by wave 3, verified here. The import now reads the file, counts the samples and shows a confirmation stating the count, that Skotiq stores eight 45° sectors keeping the tallest sample in each, the CONSEQUENCE (a sector that is really clear will be treated as blocked and the planner will skip targets there), and the eight values it is about to store; Cancel leaves the existing mask untouched. The Local Horizon Mask section itself now states the 8-sector resolution where the values are edited. The verifier's own analysis put the shippable defect in the silence, not in the numbers — the 8-sector model is the app's horizon model everywhere and the reduction is conservative.

title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
summary: NOT FIXED, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. What an earlier wave did is real but limited: the Spanish subtitle no longer claims to change 'la interfaz principal' (it now says it translates menus, navigation and Settings and that the other screens stay English), the option is labelled '(beta)', and the picker's value is the stored language code rather than a comparison of translated display strings. That is covered by general_language_scope_test.dart (3 tests, green). The DEFECT the finding names — the product surfaces are English — is a coverage program, not a defect with a removable cause: 50 of the app's ~837 source files call `l10n` at all and the catalogue holds ~498 keys, so the Dashboard body, Imaging, the Sequencer, Analytics and the persistent status bar contain hundreds of literals with no keys behind them. The two genuine resolutions are (a) finish the catalogue across those surfaces or (b) stop offering the locale; both are product decisions with costs the owner has to weigh — (b) in particular would strand anyone who already stores language='es' and would delete working translations. I deliberately did NOT ship a third partial pass (e.g. localising the status bar and the standby dashboard cards): any bounded slice leaves the finding's headline sentence — 'every other screen stays English' — true, which is the relocate-the-defect pattern this campaign penalises, and a half-Spanish status bar is not obviously better than an English one.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/general_language_scope_test.dart -> 'the Spanish option is marked partial', 'the Spanish subtitle scopes itself to what changes', 'the English subtitle keeps its scoped wording'. Green — this pins the honesty half only.
revert_check: n/a — no production change made for this item.
caveats: OWNER DECISION NEEDED: finish the es catalogue for Dashboard/Imaging/Sequencer/Analytics/status bar, or remove the locale. Until then the picker's own subtitle is the only thing keeping the claim true.

title: VERIFICATION NOTES (not a finding)
summary: Suites run green on the final tree: test/screens/shell 86/86 (app_shell + status bar), test/screens/dashboard/widgets + moon card + auto-save hydration 143/143, and the settings subsets for every already-correct verdict (41/41). Four failures in test/screens/dashboard/captures_landscape_test.dart are the @Tags(['golden']) pixel-capture harness, excluded from `melos run test` by design (dart_test.yaml + melos.yaml:318); the diff is 40.69%, a host-baseline mismatch, and the moon change is a no-op outside red night (pinned by its own test). A package-wide `flutter test` was started but is not a usable signal right now: sibling agents are running their own revert-checks in this same working tree, so skotiq_core intermittently does not compile (canPause, targetsDaoProvider, fetchAavsoAlerts, node_duration_provider, imaging_service all failed to compile at different minutes) and 14 flutter test processes are competing at load average 38. One settings-directory run reported settings_section_index_test failing; that run included the 'Backup folder' row I have since removed, and the settings tree now carries none of my changes.
